builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: GRACE: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Analysis of Closed-Form Questions over Dataframes with Guardrail Selection and Adaptive Retry
summary: Replaces single-rollout code generation and scalar-based voting with parallel best-of-N execution and artifact-based guardrail selection that can abstain when all candidates are incorrect. Costs increased API/token usage or GPU memory for concurrent agents and added system complexity for the tournament and retry logic. Can fail when guardrail validation incorrectly rejects valid answers or when the computational overhead of N parallel rollouts exceeds latency constraints.
rationale: The technique is immediately deployable on constrained infrastructure (single 24GB GPU or API-based) using the specified Qwen models, and provides a validated mechanism to significantly improve closed-form question answering accuracy while enabling explicit failure detection through abstention.
technique: Parallel Best-of-N Multi-Agent Execution with Guardrail Selection

claims.statement: Replaces single-rollout code generation and scalar-based voting with parallel best-of-N execution and artifact-based guardrail selection that can abstain when all candidates are incorrect. Costs increased API/token usage or GPU memory for concurrent agents and added system complexity for the tournament and retry logic. Can fail when guardrail validation incorrectly rejects valid answers or when the computational overhead of N parallel rollouts exceeds latency constraints.
Raises answer match from 39% to 71% (+32 pp, 1.8x) on InfiAgent-DABench using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and from 38% to 63% (+25 pp, 1.7x) with Qwen3.5-9B.
